A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same reward-adaptation research despite the changed title and algorithm names. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, although several experimental settings change.

before.justification: V1 reports original gridworld, autogenerated-MDP, Highway-City, and continuous-state experiments, including learning curves, action-pruning results, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 reports original gridworld and autogenerated-MDP experiments, including comparisons between algorithm variants, noise sensitivity, and appendix evaluations using estimated source information.

M1.justification: V1's Q-M update is retained as M-Q-M. V2 additionally introduces Q-M operators without the outer monotonic min/max restriction, allowing arbitrary initialization without source Q-variants (Section 3.2). Section 3.3 also introduces an error-aware pruning margin. These are procedural additions, beyond renaming the original method.

E1.justification: Dollar-Euro, Racetrack, Frozen Lake, and autogenerated MDPs remain. However, v2 removes Highway-City and the appendix Cartpole, Lunar Lander, and Pong evaluations. It also removes the distinct autogenerated scenario with randomized transition rewards. This substantially narrows the evaluated domains and reward scenarios.

E2.justification: V2 adds Soft Q Bounding (SQB) alongside retained QL and SFQL in the gridworld and autogenerated comparisons (Figures 2 and 4). The noise comparison retains QL but drops SFQL (v1 Figure 6 versus v2 Figure 5). These materially revise the evaluated comparator sets; the changed year of the successor-features citation does not introduce a different SFQL baseline.

E3.justification: Autogenerated designed-reward experiments change from randomly sized MDPs to 60 states and 9 actions, and the shared terminal source rewards change from 0.5 to 0.6. The linear experiment's SBF settings change from 1/5/9 to 1/3/5. Noise testing changes from 0/25/50% relative to mean rewards to 0.25–1.25% relative to Rmax=1.2. V2 also adds estimated-source-information comparisons within the retained domains.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct Q-M versus M-Q-M pruning analysis, quantifies pruning under noise, and examines estimated lite-models, rewards, and Q-variants (Sections 4.3.1, 4.5, and A.4). The appendix identifies erroneous optimal-action pruning in Racetrack. These substantially extend mechanism and failure analysis, while v1's Highway-City case study and discretization analysis disappear.

E5.justification: Both versions report 30 runs. V2 explicitly identifies convergence-plot shading as 95% confidence intervals; v1 shows shaded bands without identifying their statistical meaning. V1's detailed runtime and pruning tables with means and standard deviations are removed. There is no reported increase in run count.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for the new Q-M variant, SQB, and estimated-information M-Q-M_p, including suboptimal Racetrack convergence. Figure 5 newly reports 17.1% versus 7.4% pruning for M-Q-M versus Q-M at 0.25% noise. Removed-domain results and five full runtime-comparison tables disappear. Autogenerated curves and iteration times are revised under changed settings, so they do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 adds strict-contraction and unique-fixed-point results for the new Q-M operators, an ordering theorem establishing valid limiting bounds, and corresponding appendix proofs (Theorems 3.4–3.5). It also adds sample-complexity and regret reasoning in Section 3.1.2 and an error-based pruning threshold. Much of v1's convergence, initialization, and optimality theory remains under the M-Q-M terminology.

C1.justification: V1 pairs optimality-preserving pruning with empirically demonstrated sample-efficiency gains. V2 elevates sample efficiency to a claimed probabilistic theoretical guarantee, explicitly claims resistance to negative transfer, and presents two algorithms as its central contribution. These materially strengthen and expand the abstract and introduction claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains why source-initialized M-Q-M can prune more than Q-M and attributes the practical Racetrack failure to inaccurate source Q-values. Its new limitations section discusses unsafe worst-policy learning, initialization quality, continuous-space approximation errors, and reward-relationship assumptions. Section 3.1.1 also qualifies expressivity relative to SFQL when the combination function is restricted.

D1.justification: V2 adds an anonymous code-access link, explicitly describes transition-support memorization requirements, and specifies value iteration for SFQL policy evaluation. It documents the pruning tolerance relationship while retaining the same laptop and broad Q-learning hyperparameter information. Tile-coding/DQN instructions and detailed runtime-accounting disclosures disappear with the removed experiments.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused around transfer-learning assumptions, negative transfer, and lite-models, with a new Q-M/SFQL/SQB comparison table. V2 adds relevant positioning through Adamczyk, Taylor and Stone, Wulfmeier, Qu and Wierman, and other works, while substantially shortening the earlier reward-decomposition, multi-objective, and hierarchical-RL discussions.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and extensively reorganized. Related work moves before the method; methodology is divided into preliminaries and two algorithm variants; experiments are regrouped; and a dedicated limitations section is added. Introduction, contribution, and related-work prose undergo substantial rewriting beyond simple renumbering.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text from two columns to one, reorganizes convergence plots, places revised pruning heatmaps in the main text, and adds a noise-pruning bar chart. A method-comparison table is introduced. Highway-City and continuous-state figures and five detailed runtime tables are removed, while the iteration-time table is retained in revised form.

improvement.justification: The new operator proofs, SQB comparisons, explicit confidence intervals, and approximation-failure analysis strengthen v2. However, it removes broad-domain evidence and most full-runtime comparisons while making stronger efficiency claims. Section 3.1.2 asserts that mixing time typically decreases without establishing its behavior after pruning, leaving the headline guarantee incompletely justified within the PDFs. These material benefits and weaknesses prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
